scope: Bounded primary-source review for 5D hypercube counts, orthogonal coordinate-plane rotations, known-transform linear observability, and closed 5D-ball 3D slices
execution_policy: Read-only source inspection. No implementation, browser run, deployment, external communication, human study, Gate 6 work, or publication.

primary_sources.title: Lecture 11: High Dimensional Geometry, Curse of Dimensionality, Dimension Reduction
primary_sources.author: Sanjeev Arora, Princeton University COS 521
pins: PDF p. 1, fetched lines 26-39: the unit n-cube in R^n is {(x1,...,xn): 0 <= xi <= 1}.
PDF p. 1, fetched lines 40-44: the unit n-ball is B_n = {x : sum_i x_i^2 <= 1}.
PDF p. 1, fetched lines 45-53: the x_1=1/2 slice of the 4D unit ball is a 3-ball of radius sqrt(1-(1/2)^2), and every parallel slice is a ball.
supports: The Euclidean closed-ball equation used as the source definition for the 5D slice derivation.
A fixed-coordinate slice reduces the dimension by one and has a square-root residual radius; the two-fixed-coordinate 5D case follows by direct substitution.
does_not_support: The project’s centered {-1,+1}^5 vertex convention; the 32/80 count is derived in this review.
The project’s coordinate-plane rotation matrices, projection matrix, UI, or camera behavior.
A browser, human-comprehension, arbitrary-reconstruction, or physical-extra-dimension claim.
primary_sources.use_in_gate5: Reused verified prior primary ball source for the 5D closed-ball equation and the dimension-drop/square-root slice law.

primary_sources.title: NumCS(E), AT’25, Chapter 3: Direct Methods for Linear Least Squares Problems
primary_sources.author: Ralf Hiptmair, ETH Zurich
pins: PDF p. 25, fetched lines 2577-2586: Q is orthogonal when Q^{-1}=Q^T, and orthogonal/unitary maps preserve the Euclidean 2-norm.
PDF p. 12, fetched lines 1397-1408: if m >= n and N(A)={0}, least squares has a unique solution; N(A)={0} is equivalent to rank(A)=n.
PDF p. 13, fetched lines 1489-1492: rank defect means redundant parameters can yield the same outputs and are not observable/identifiable.
supports: Orthogonal coordinate-plane rotation blocks preserve source norms and pairwise distances.
For a stacked known linear observation system, full column rank is the condition for unique least-squares recovery.
A rank-deficient observation leaves at least one source-coordinate direction unidentifiable under the declared model.
does_not_support: The specific x-w and y-v matrices, fixed P=[I_3 0 0], or the project’s composition order; these are direct derivations/model choices.
Recovery from arbitrary screenshots, unknown transforms/correspondences, a physical five-dimensional space, or human comprehension.
primary_sources.use_in_gate5: Primary linear-algebra reference for orthogonality, rank, unique least-squares recovery, and the meaning of hidden/unidentifiable coordinates.

derived_checks.derivation: Each of five coordinates independently takes two values; each vertex has five one-coordinate neighbors and each undirected edge is counted at both endpoints.
derived_checks.status: direct derivation under the declared centered hypercube model from the Princeton n-cube definition

derived_checks.derivation: Each matrix is identity outside a 2-by-2 rotation block; direct multiplication gives R^T R=I. The planes are disjoint, so the two matrices commute, with inverses at negated angles.
derived_checks.status: direct matrix derivation, with orthogonality/norm preservation interpreted using the ETH source

derived_checks.claim: Known 5D linear observation reaches rank five
derived_checks.formula: p=P R_yv(b) R_xw(a) q, P=[I_3 0 0]; identity view plus a=b=pi/2 has row span {e_x,e_y,e_z,-e_w,-e_v}
derived_checks.derivation: A single view has at most three rows. With x-w-only views, the v column is zero and rank is at most four. Adding the known y-v rotation supplies the v row, giving rank five and conditional unique least-squares recovery.
derived_checks.status: direct linear-algebra derivation plus the ETH full-column-rank result

derived_checks.derivation: Substitute the two fixed coordinates into x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2+v^2<=R^2. Positive residual gives a solid 3-ball, zero gives one point, and negative residual gives empty.
derived_checks.status: direct derivation from the Princeton n-ball definition; two-constraint extension is project-derived

derived_checks.formula: rho(s,t) depends only on s^2+t^2; e.g. for R=1, (0.6,0) and (0,0.6) both give rho=0.8
derived_checks.derivation: Distinct parameter pairs on the same circle in the (s,t) plane have equal residual radius and therefore equal centered 3D slice geometry.
derived_checks.status: project-derived bounded ambiguity; equal geometry does not identify ordered hidden parameters without metadata or intervention

limits: The rank-five check assumes exact known linear transforms, known point correspondences, the fixed coordinate projection, and numerical tolerance; it is not arbitrary image inversion.
The 5D slice assumes a centered Euclidean closed ball and two coordinate hyperplanes. Translated or tilted planes require a corresponding distance-to-center derivation.
The equal-radius ambiguity concerns the declared centered-ball slice geometry; source metadata can distinguish parameter pairs even when their displayed geometry is equal.
No source supports a browser result, human understanding, arbitrary reconstruction, or a physical-extra-dimension claim.
